Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Config, laid out from one table of settings**: a game adds a setting with `KAGDefineOption` and the Config screen, Default and saving follow (`doc/kagex.txt`, "Options and the Config Screen"). The sample's Config has four pages: the first as before, Voices and Saves, Reading, and Screen and Extras
- **Reading settings**: the window's opacity, a colour and a click mark for read text, text that fades in, read-text and auto-mode speeds, auto waits that grow with the line, a pause after a voice in auto mode, a dramatic mode that hides the window while a voice plays, a pointer that hides when still, and "Don't ask again" on the save, load and title prompts
- **The hero's name**: the first START asks for it, refusing names too long or on the game's list, and the lines, the name box, the backlog and Search use it (`kag.setHeroName`, `"&kag.heroName()"`)
- **A name box that fits and fades**: a long name squeezes into its box, the box fades and crossfades between speakers and follows the window's opacity (`[position namefit=squeeze namefade=150 followopacity=true]`)
- **On-screen indicators**: a chapter's title in a corner (`[chapter]`, or each compiled scene's title), the music's title when it changes, an auto/skip mark and a voice bar, each switchable in Config
- **Movies as commercial games handle them**: `[movie]` can't be skipped until seen, stops skip mode before a new movie, unlocks its song in the music room, fills a colour behind it and plays a smaller version on the web and phones, with **subtitles** from a WebVTT file per language. The sample opens with a short movie, and Replay has a Movies tab
- **A credits roll** timed to the rest of the music (`fliptype=roll`, from a text file with headings, gaps and pictures), skippable once seen; the demo menu has Credits
- **For writers**: `[ai 102]` sets a pose and a face through `"shorthands"` in `envinit.tjs`, `[ai far]`/`[ai near]` change depth and order at once, and `[vo ai000003]` plays a voice file and works out whose line it is (`doc/world.txt`)
- **Extras**: counts of CGs found, the tab last used, the music room's track playing on through CG and Replay (and on the title if kept), and an evening title unlocked by finishing every demo
- **kagex-release**: the Android manifest gets the query for the system's text-to-speech engines and a game's own additions (`platforms.android.manifestAdditions`, `applicationAdditions`)
- kagex-release 0.17.0 downloads the 0.17.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.17.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
